text.p: A typhoid fever epidemic raging through the troubled former Soviet republic of Tajikistan has claimed more than 80 lives, a western aid source said on Friday.

The source told Reuters by telephone from Dushanbe that 37 people had died in hospitals in the Tajik capital alone while at least another 50 had died from the fever elsewhere in the rugged Central Asian state bordering China and Afghanistan.
"The typhoid epidemic is spreading pretty fast," said Bandisho Shoyismatullayev, head of Tajikistan's sanitary and epidemiological inspectorate.
He said some 4,000 cases had been registered. But aid workers said the number of those infected was probably at least twice as high.
Local and foreign medical workers say the poor quality of the water supply for most of the 5.7 million population is behind the outbreak of the disease.
The International Federation of the Red Cross said earlier this week that the cash-strapped Tajik government had not chlorinated Dushanbe's water supply for three months.
Tajikistan, devastated by a bloody four-year civil war, suffered a typhoid epidemic last year, affecting only southern regions of the country, but infecting 6,000 and killing 260.
Aid workers say the authorities had failed to take the necessary measures to prevent this year's epidemic.
Talks between government and Islamic opposition officials continued in Moscow on Friday. They are discussing military terms to end the war after signing a peace accord in December.
